summary: A two-column Sankey diagram, sources on the left flowing into uses on the right: ribbon widths from a row-major float array the host can replace, every ribbon, bar and label easing to new data together, optional particles flowing along each ribbon at a speed proportional to its flow, and each node labelled with its total.

flows.doc: A float array ("@name" of resources.floatArrays, exported so the host can replace it), row-major: flows[s * uses + u] is what source s sends to use u; zeros are fine (no ribbon)

sources.doc: Left-column nodes in order: "Solar", or {"label": "Solar", "color": "@colors.solar"}, or [label, color]; colours default to theme colours

unit.doc: Appended to every node total (keep the leading space)

whole.doc: Integer digits kept in the totals (textFromFloat whole: 2 shows up to 99)

anim.doc: Seconds a change of data eases over (0: jump); also the grow-in at load. Not in mono

particles.doc: Dots flowing along each ribbon (not in mono, which does not repaint continuously)

speed.doc: Particle trips per second per unit of flow

dotColor.doc: Particle colour (drawn at 85 % fading in and out at the bars)

fill.doc: Fill the space the caller gives it; false: fillMaxWidth x height

height.doc: Height in dp when fill is false

pitfalls: flows is the NAME of a float array with sources x uses values, row-major; a wrong length draws missing ribbons as zero rather than failing
Totals are the sums of the ribbons: a node that both receives and sends (a battery charging and discharging) needs to be split into a source and a use
The particle speed reads the raw host value while the ribbons ease, so on a data change the dots jump once to their new phase
Each ribbon costs about 400 B and each particle loop about 300 B: 3 x 4 nodes is about 9 KB with particles, 6 KB without; keep the node count small
Particles use continuousSec(): the diagram repaints every frame while shown; particles: false makes it idle once the data settles
Mono: ribbons become outlines over a faint fill and the bars ink; node colours carry no meaning there, the labels do
